valley noun

classical

Traupman 401

vallis, vallis f.

noun, third declension

Both nominatives are classical, vallis and vallēs; Lewis & Short and Traupman give vallēs first, and so do we.

Other words

  • vallēs, vallis f.

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 7.47; Verg. A. 11.522 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 206, 401; Andresian p. 22; Traupman 207

    The same word with a nominative in -ēs, Caesar’s form; Lewis & Short and Traupman give it first.

  • convallis, convallis f. — enclosed valley

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · L&S

Examples

  • hoc pecus omne meum est, multae quoque vallibus errant, multās silva tegit, multae stabulantur in antrīs

    this whole flock is mine; many more wander in the valleys, many are hidden in the woods, many are penned in cavesOv. Met. 13.821–822

See also mountain, plain.
